item.title: 2 Detroit Lions Will Almost Certainly Miss Germany Game
item.description: The Detroit Lions received some encouraging injury news Wednesday as they prepare for Sunday’s matchup against the New England Patriots in Germany. However, head coach Dan Campbell also revealed that two key starters remain unlikely to play. According to Wednesday’s update, Campbell said defensive end DJ Wonnum is expected to return to practice after missing Sunday’s 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins with a concussion. As long as Wonnum avoids any setbacks, Campbell believes he should be available against New England. Unfortunately, the news wasn’t nearly as promising for center Cade Mays and cornerback D.J. Reed. Neither player is expected to practice Wednesday, and Campbell indicated that both are doubtful at best for Sunday’s game. Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray (1) almost has his pass blocked by Detroit Lions edge rusher DJ Wonnum (98) that lead to an incomplete pass on the third down, during the first half of the N.F.L. game at Ford Field in Detroit, Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit Lions Could Get DJ Wonnum Back Wonnum’s potential return would provide an important boost to Detroit’s defensive front. The veteran pass rusher was among five Lions ruled out against Miami , leaving Detroit shorthanded on defense. According to the Lions’ official November 6 injury report , Wonnum did not practice last week while dealing with his concussion. Wednesday’s expected return represents an encouraging development, although his availability remains dependent on avoiding setbacks and receiving the necessary clearance. Meanwhile, the outlook for Mays and Reed remains concerning. Both players were already expected to miss last Sunday’s game , and neither appears particularly close to returning. Mays continues to deal with an ankle injury, while Reed is recovering from a hip injury. According to the Lions’ official inactive report against Miami , veteran Juice Scruggs started at center in Mays’ absence, while Detroit relied on its secondary depth without Reed. The Lions will continue monitoring all three players throughout the week before making final decisions on their availability. For now, Wonnum appears to be trending in the right direction, while Mays and Reed face an uphill battle to suit up against the Patriots.

item.title: Skip Bayless says Carson Wentz ‘can’t play football’ after Vikings performance vs Bills
item.description: Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images Carson Wentz’s performance on Monday Night Football drew heavy criticism from everyone in the NFL community, and Skip Bayless joined in by going off on the quarterback. The 33-year-old threw for 81 yards and completed only 8 passes out of 25 attempts, which meant he had a completion rate of only 32%. Wentz ended up with a passer rating of 8.9, which is the lowest for any player with 25 or more passes in the NFL since 2019. His inability to get the ball to the end zone led the Vikings to suffer a 6-23 defeat and pushed them out of the top place in the NFC North. This was Wentz’s chance to prove that he could take over Kyler Murray as the starter, but he put on a horrific performance, which led to the Vikings deciding to trade for Kirk Cousins at the trade deadline, which was just a day after the game. Skip Bayless believes Carson Wentz is not accurate consistently Wentz was a regular starter in the league for 7 seasons. He was a second pick in the 2016 draft by the Philadelphia Eagles; however, he was never able to fulfil the promise he showed at North Dakota State. In the games he has started, Wentz has thrown for over 23,000 yards and completed 62.7% of his passes. But none of that impressed Bayless, who fired shots at Wentz, discussing his performance on Monday Night Football. “I have been hard on him. I was hard on Carson Wentz coming out of college before he got drafted. I didn’t like him at North Dakota State. I didn’t like his poise or his feel. He’s one of those guys who’s the prototype 6’5, 240-pound, rocket-arm quarterback who can’t play football, and he’s not accurate consistently. All he can do is throw it through a brick wall. Well, that’s not how you win NFL games at the highest level,” said Bayless on Gridiron. With Cousins now set to take over the reins as the starting quarterback, Wentz’s future with the Vikings could be questionable. They already have Kyler Murray, who can play as the backup. He is definitely a good piece to have on a team, as he has proven experience starting games, which not a lot of backups in the league have. However, after his performance against the Bills, fans would definitely not be happy if they see him take snaps under center. item.title: Are the Wizards Asking Too Much of Kyshawn George?
item.description: The Washington Wizards have been trying to understand what their young roster can become. Kyshawn George is making a strong case for a big role with the Wizards, but his recent performances have also raised questions about whether the Wizards are putting too much responsibility on him too soon. George has shown that he can help this team in several areas of the game. The 6-foot-7 forward has become a key piece of the Wizards’ offense, using his scoring ability and creative playmaking to make opportunities for himself and his teammates. Over the last few games, George has become particularly encouraging. George scored 22 points against the Orlando Magic on Nov. 2, followed by 25 points facing the Atlanta Hawks on Nov. 4. He then dropped 33 points in another loss to Atlanta the next game, adding eight assists and five three-pointers. Those numbers show why Washington has continued to give George opportunities with the ball in his hands. However, his development isn’t just about scoring and how many points he can score. The Wizards also need to find the right role for him as he continues to improve in the NBA. He’s been able to score, defend multiple positions, and help create offense for his teammates. Washington has also been experimenting with using him as a point guard when Trae Young is not playing. That responsibility has not always been easy. George recorded eight turnovers against the Toronto Raptors on Oct. 23, a performance that showed some of the challenges of asking him to run the Wizards’ offense. He has the ability to make plays, but becoming a good ball handler takes time. After George’s 22-point performance on the Chicago Bulls defense on Oct. 24, Wizards coach Brian Keefe discussed his ability to create more opportunities by getting into the paint. “You saw him being able to create and get into the paint,” Keefe said. “A lot more paint touches for us tonight, which we wanted to emphasize, and he was a catalyst for that.” The comments, reported by Roundtable Sports , show that Washington finds value in what George can bring when he is attacking the basket instead of forcing himself to make all of the plays. item.title: Marcus Rashford races to be fit for Liverpool trip as Man Utd put new recovery programme in place for his groin problem
item.description: Manchester United v Tottenham Hotspur - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United are hopeful Marcus Rashford will be fit for their trip to Liverpool a week on Sunday after the forward began a new treatment programme on a groin problem. The 29-year-old has missed United's last six games, but a visit to a specialist in Dublin has given the club fresh optimism ahead of a clash against the rivals he has so often hurt. Specialist visit sparks fresh hope Manchester United hope Rashford will be available for their next game at Liverpool a week on Sunday after he started a new recovery programme, according to the Daily Mail . The forward travelled to Dublin last week with a member of the club's medical staff to see a groin specialist, and a fresh plan is now in place. Rashford picked up a hip injury at the World Cup before returning to Old Trafford in the summer following a season on loan at Barcelona. He has since missed United's last six games after the problem was aggravated and spread to his groin. Rashford offered to play through the pain Rashford featured in the first six league games of the season, as well as the Carabao Cup tie against Brighton and the Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid in mid-October. He is said to have a good relationship with Michael Carrick and wanted to support the head coach during a difficult spell. However, playing while carrying the injury only made it worse. It is understood Rashford even offered to go on the bench for last month's defeat at Chelsea, but United decided it was not worth the risk of further damage. Impressive record against Liverpool Rashford is yet to score for United since his return from Barcelona, but his record against Liverpool offers real cause for optimism. The England international has scored seven goals in 20 appearances against United's biggest rivals, which makes him a valuable option for the trip to Anfield. He will continue to work his way back to fitness during the international break, with United hopeful he will be ready for the game on November 22. His return would be a timely lift for a squad that has been missing one of its most experienced attackers. What comes next for Rashford and United? The Liverpool clash could also mark the start of a new era at Old Trafford. The report adds that Carrick is expected to be sacked and replaced by Mauricio Pochettino, which means the trip to Anfield could be his first game in charge. Pochettino would be returning to the Premier League after previous spells at Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton.

item.title: Shrewsbury 'hit all the boxes' for new owners - Friedel
item.description: Shrewsbury Town are 15th in League Two [Getty Images] Shrewsbury Town's new sporting director Brad Friedel says the club is the perfect project for the US-backed owners after a Europe-wide search ended with them taking contol of the League Two outfit. Scott Davidson's Biscayne ST LLC consortium, which Friedel is part of, completed their takeover on Monday, buying 87.4% of the shares and allowing long-time owner Roland Wycherley to relinquish control. "Scott and I met through friends in Miami and through the love of football and nothing more or less," former Blackburn and USA goalkeeper Friedel told BBC Radio Shropshire in an exclusive interview. "As we got to know each other, our thoughts on business and football aligned - we got to the point where we said let's try to find a club which fits a whole bunch of criteria. "So we looked in Turkey, Poland, Portugal and Holland but the clubs we were looking at, something didn't align for one reason or another and a lot of it came down to did we think our group can help the football club because we want to bring the town firmly behind the club." Wycherley first announced his plans to find a successor five years ago and Friedel says with Davidson already being a majority shareholder of Edinburgh-based The Spartans in Scottish League Two, they wanted a club they could take forward both on and off the field. "The one-town club really appealed to us because we want to intergrate the club even more into the town than it is now and when you look at the investment going into the EFL, the foreign investment going into it, there's a reason for it because there's no better place for football than the United Kingdom. "Once we decided our group would be best suited to the UK market, Shrewsbury hit all the boxes of what we like, but also what we feel we can deliver towards the club and the town." Shrewsbury takeover in 'final stages' - Wycherley Friedel group completes Shrewsbury Town takeover As a player, Friedel spent the majority of his career in the Premier League with Liverpool, Blackburn, Aston Villa and Tottenham, but the 55-year-old is unfazed about taking his first sporting director role in England's fourth tier. "I don't look at football anymore as I would only take a job in the Premier League or the Champions League," he said. "One of my most enjoyable jobs post-playing career was being head coach of the US men's under-19 national team and most of those players weren't even professional. "I look at football opportunities with different projects. The upside if you get it right in English football is there is such a buzz for me out of it, so I don't look at this as an EFL League Two club, I look at is as another incredible project with incredible people." item.description: Nov 10, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Los Angeles Clippers guard Darius Garland (10) passes the ball against Phoenix Suns guard Devin Booker (15) in the second half at Mortgage Matchup Center. Whatever good feeling the Clippers carried out of Sunday's win over New Orleans was gone by the end of the first quarter in Phoenix, where the Suns closed the period on a 13-0 run and cruised to a 133-110 win at Mortgage Matchup Center. Phoenix made 22 of 43 attempts from 3-point range, a season high, and got 81 points from a bench that had five players finish in double figures. The Clippers fell to 2-8 overall and 0-5 on the road, with eight losses in their last nine games. Jordan Goodwin did most of the early damage in his first game back from a calf injury, making six of his seven 3-point tries for 18 points in 14 minutes. Devin Booker added 17 points and five assists for a Suns team that lost by 26 to San Antonio the night before. The Game Got Away Early The Clippers held a brief lead late in the first quarter, going up 18-16 before the Phoenix second unit took the game over with the 13-0 run that ended the period. Goodwin had 15 points by halftime, Luke Kennard hit a pair of 3-pointers off the bench and Collin Gillespie hit a 39-footer at the buzzer that sent Phoenix to the locker room up 64-47. The Suns made 11 of their 22 attempts from deep in the first half, a pace the Clippers had no answer for on either end. The third quarter went even worse for Los Angeles, with the Suns stretching the lead to 91-59 and taking a 99-72 edge into the fourth. Phoenix sat all five starters for the final period, so the 38-34 fourth quarter the Clippers won against an all-reserve group did little beyond trimming the final margin. item.title: Dan Campbell Sends Clear Message After Lions’ Quiet NFL Trade Deadline
item.description: The Detroit Lions didn’t make the splash many fans were hoping for at Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, but head coach Dan Campbell doesn’t appear to be losing any sleep over it. In fact, Campbell sounds pretty confident about the roster general manager Brad Holmes has assembled. Speaking to reporters Wednesday, Campbell was asked about Detroit’s lack of activity and how he feels about his team heading into the stretch run of the season. His response was simple, and it certainly didn’t sound like a coach who believes his team is missing a major piece. “Feel good. We love our guys, man. We love our guys. …I think we’re in a good spot here, man,” Campbell said, according to The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy. That’s a pretty strong endorsement considering the Lions’ decision to stand pat while other NFL contenders made significant additions. Brad Galli of WXYZ-TV added that Campbell believes the Lions identified opportunities to improve internally early in the season, particularly on defense. And judging by Detroit’s recent performances, the head coach believes that improvement is happening. “When you’re doing that, it’s like ‘That’s what we thought it would be,'” Campbell explained. “A lot of things were looked at, but we feel pretty good right now.” The Lions have won four consecutive games to improve to 6-2, and their defense has taken noticeable strides during that stretch. That improvement appears to be a major reason Campbell feels comfortable moving forward with the players already in the building. item.title: Aston Villa confirm another star has extended contract
item.description: Aston Villa confirm another star has extended contract Ian Maatsen has penned a new contract at Aston Villa until 2032, and says he is keen to kick on under boss Unai Emery having already established himself as a key player. Maatsen extended his stay at Villa Park on Wednesday, having arrived at the club in the summer of 2024. The left-back discussed his relationship with manager Unai Emery, and what made him keen to continue at Villa Park. “First of all, the way the club is progressing, in a good way,” he said. “A big part of this way is the coach, the vision he sees in this club, and everyone around him, and also my teammates. “I really enjoy it. He’s really demanding, but he’s a very good coach who really gets into the details. “He wants to make sure everyone is on the same page with the same plan, and it works. It’s a very good relationship. “I feel at home here and I can develop here. It motivates me to bring this club to special things with them, and that’s the reason I signed the contract.” Asked on his favourite memories in claret and blue so far, last season’s Europa League final and subsequent trophy parade sticks out for Maatsen, who was proud to be able to help the Villa faithful create special memories. The Netherlands international added: “On the pitch is probably the Europa League final. A big trophy for the club. “We hadn’t won [a trophy] in many years, so it was a good contribution for us as a team and a group, but also for the fans, for the club itself. “The parade, to celebrate with the fans, the people in Birmingham, the local people, it was a very special day. “It felt good. You see how big Birmingham is and we have a lot of Aston Villa fans. It’s good for the city to celebrate with us, so it was an amazing day.” Confirmation of Maatsen’s new deal comes after Victor Lindelof also extended his stay at the club .

item.title: Houston Comets president shares which WNBA player would be the ‘ultimate dream’
item.description: Photo by Erica Denhoff/NurPhoto via Getty Images Jennifer Rizzotti is looking ahead to the Houston Comets’ return to the WNBA. The Houston Comets are at a turning point right now as they get ready to step back onto the WNBA court. Coming off the relocation of the Connecticut Sun franchise, the team finds itself right in the middle of the draft lottery following a tough 2026 season. But there’s plenty of reason for optimism, as Houston is tied for the top odds at 32.9% to land the No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to the lottery rules, they can’t drop past third, giving them a real shot to draft a superstar and kick off this new chapter right away. Jennifer Rizzotti would love a player like A’ja Wilson Speaking on the team’s mindset, Houston Comets President Jennifer Rizzotti laid out exactly what she wants in their next draft pick. For her, she wants someone like A’ja Wilson , who brings an unmatched work ethic and leadership that can reshape an entire franchise from day one. “You know, obviously, you know, when you look at like who’s done it the best, you’ve got to look at A’ja Wilson, right? And we, you know, we can’t all get A’ja Wilsons, but you hope that you’ll continue to have players like her. They’re—they’re great when they come out of college already. “However, they have a work ethic that will, you know, supersede just talent, right? So she wanted to not just be the best coming out of college, but she wanted to be the best period. And then you add on top of it her leadership, right? You watch how she talks to her teammates, how she treats her teammates, how much they respect her, and how they play for her. “Like, that’s like the ultimate dream if you can get a player like A’ja Wilson into your organization. They don’t grow on trees, though, right? So, so then for us, like, we, you know, we’re hoping to have a pretty high draft pick because we’re in the lottery.” A’ja Wilson has solidified her spot among the all-time greats, bringing home a record-extending fifth WNBA MVP, her third in a row. She put together a crazy season, leading the league with 26.2 points per game and becoming the first player ever to post back-to-back 1,000-point years. Beyond the numbers, her relentless drive and locker-room leadership are why she’s the absolute gold standard for what a WNBA superstar looks like today. item.title: Aday Mara’s Strong Development Defends Against OKC Injuries
item.description: Nov 7, 2026; Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, USA; Oklahoma City Thunder center Aday Mara (15) celebrates after dunking against the Washington Wizards during the second half at Paycom Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jimmy Vik Aday Mara is on the rise for the Oklahoma City Thunder this season, and the team hopes that he can continue his development throughout the campaign. Suddenly thrown into the fire, it does seem that the big man is filling the gap in OKC’s defensive needs. He’s also shining on offense, which is definitely something they need with multiple key stars out with injuries for the Thunder . From deterring opponents from scoring, blocking shots, crashing the glass, and even creating offensive opportunities, Mara has been a standout for Oklahoma City. He’s providing a spark that you wouldn’t expect from a rookie. Now he’s proven that he can be a consistent player for the team, and that’s the hope for him moving forward. Mara Has Been a Beast for the Thunder Nov 7, 2026; Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, USA; Oklahoma City Thunder center Aday Mara (15) dunks against the Washington Wizards during the second half at Paycom Center. Mandatory Credit: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images Now averaging 8.3 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 1.8 blocks per game this season, it’s clear that Mara has excelled off OKC’s bench . His numbers have gone up, and he has garnered a higher usage rate than ever. That says a lot for someone who’s supposed to be getting fewer touches as a reserve before getting acclimated to bigger minutes. But with the Chet Holmgren injury , the Thunder’s center spot finds itself with a vacant hole — something that Mara is now taking over in the star’s absence. We are at a point where the Spanish center is showcasing his skill set well. ADAY MARA WILL NOT BE DENIED 😤 STICKS WITH IT FOR THE TWO-HAND JAM! pic.twitter.com/txrcvcClmY — NBA (@NBA) November 11, 2026 At seven-foot-three, OKC getting Mara in the draft was a huge boon for the franchise on both sides. He’s got the potential to be a high-impact defensive anchor alongside Holmgren, which is on-brand with the Thunder’s identity. Let’s not forget the fact that he’s just 21 as well. Rebounding Gets a Boost from Mara As a big man, you’d expect Mara to be a hulk on the glass, much like Victor Wembanyama . This month, the Thunder center has finished with more than five boards in his games. He’s averaging 7.8 rebounds in this month alone. If that’s not eye-catching enough for you, then it’s worth noting that Mara’s rebounding has been essential for the Thunder. In fact, thanks to his efforts, through 11 games, OKC is grabbing nearly five more defensive rebounds per game without Holmgren than with him (36.9 to 32.7). Of course, no Holmgren means Mara and Isaiah Hartenstein get more share at the center spot. item.title: Breno Sales hails Brazil U17s' collective strength ahead of World Cup
item.description: Breno Sales hails Brazil U17s' collective strength ahead of World Cup Breno Sales in action for Brazil U-17 Credits: Fabio Souza /CBF Winning the U-17 World Cup and bringing the trophy home to Brazil: that is the goal for Breno Sales and the other players called up by coach Carlos Eduardo Patetuci. The Vasco centre-back sees individual quality, intensity and team spirit as some of Brazil's main strengths heading into the tournament, which will be held in Qatar. “We have just one goal: to become champions and bring this World Cup home to Brazil. God willing, we'll have a good tournament and come out on top,” he said. Breno believes that the ability to win individual duels, combined with the determination to win possession and total commitment during matches, could make the difference in Brazil's campaign. Breno Sales, Brazil U-17 centre-back Credits: Fabio Souza /CBF “We have individual skill, quality in one-on-one situations, determination and unity. We run all the time, we never stop running, and we're always looking to win possession and keep the ball,” he explained. Another factor the defender considers important is the experience shared within the squad. Having players who have already had opportunities in professional football allows for an exchange of knowledge that, he says, helps the whole group mature. “It's important to seek their advice and listen to what they have to say. It's an exchange. We learn from them and also try to help a little,” he explained. Born in 2009, Breno also values the bonds built over successive call-ups. The centre-back believes that understanding one another helps the team cope with pressure and gives the players greater confidence on the pitch. “We always try to help each other, regardless of the moment or the circumstances. That makes things easier, because it takes some of the pressure out of the game. It also reduces the fear of making mistakes, since we're all together, supporting each other,” he said. Being called up for the World Cup marks a special achievement in the player's career. Breno celebrated the news with his family and highlighted what it means to represent his country in a competition of this magnitude. “Every child who plays football dreams of having the chance to play in an U-17 World Cup. I celebrated with my family. It was a dream and, thank God, I'm getting to fulfil it. Wearing the Brazil shirt is something that really touches my heart,” he revealed. Brazil are in Group I of the U-17 World Cup alongside Ireland, Tanzania and Costa Rica. The team will make their debut on November 21 against Ireland. item.title: Barcelona prioritise January move for €20 million-rated teenage defender – report
item.description: Barcelona prioritise January move for €20 million-rated teenage defender – report According to Ferran Correas of SPORT , Barcelona have decided to go after the signing of FC Twente defender Ruud Nijstad in the upcoming January transfer window as a priority. Director Deco and the Barcelona sporting department want to strengthen Hansi Flick’s defensive options, and the 18-year-old Dutchman remains high on their list despite the financial obstacles involved. Barcelona want a new defender Barcelona opted not to sign a new central defender in the summer despite letting go of Ronald Araujo and Alvaro Cortes. However, the injuries to Andreas Christensen, Eric Garcia, and Jules Kounde exposed the lack of depth in the position, leaving Flick short on options. Even though Christensen is back, Barcelona’s position on signing a reinforcement has not changed, as the club continue to see Garcia and Kounde as primarily options in the right-back position. Barcelona ready to go after Nijstad again. (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images for DFB) It leaves the manager with only Pau Cubarsi, Gerard Martin and an injury-prone Christensen as main options at the heart of the backline. As such, Barcelona have made the decision to go after a new centre-back in January, with the preference being to sign someone with a long-term view rather than a stop-gap fix for only the second half of the season. Nijstad emerges as the preferred option And, even though there have been links to several players such as Natan of Real Betis and Manchester United star Lisandro Martinez, Nijstad has emerged as the priority target for Barcelona . The Blaugrana made contact to explore a move for the defender last summer, but nothing materialised as Nijstad, who also attracted interest from other major European clubs, opted to stay at Twente. The 18-year-old defender has a contract with the Dutch club running until June 2029, and his performances have pushed his valuation upwards. Deco does not want to spend €20 million on Nijstad. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) As such, Twente are looking for a transfer fee of around €20 million for the teenage centre-back, a figure Barcelona are unwilling to meet. The Blaugrana appreciate the youngster’s profile and value his immense potential, but see the transfer fee being quoted as higher than what they intend to spend. Moreover, there is also the difficulty of Financial Fair Play, as the Catalans only have a margin of around €3-4 million. While that may have improved following Raphinha’s renewal, it still restricts the club’s spending power. As such, the future of Alejandro Balde, who is linked with a January exit, could play a key role in Barcelona’s pursuit of Nijstad.

item.title: Ex-Red Sox Reliever, Braves World Series Champion Retires After 11-Year MLB Career
item.description: retired pitcher Chris Martin Longtime reliever Chris Martin has retired after 11 seasons in the big leagues, according to MLB insider Robert Murray. Martin pitched for seven organizations, but spent the most time with the Texas Rangers. He also pitched for the Colorado Rockies, New York Yankees, Atlanta Braves, Chicago Cubs, Los Angeles Dodgers and Boston Red Sox. Martin won a World Series with the Braves in 2021, pitching in five games during their run to the Fall Classic. He allowed just one run that postseason across 4 1/3 innings. He pitched in three postseasons for the Braves and one for the Dodgers. The Rockies drafted Martin in 2005, but he did not make his debut until 2014, at 27 years old. He appeared in 16 games that season and was traded to the Yankees before the 2015 season. The Yankees released him after the 2015 season, and he spent the 2016 and 2017 seasons in Japan. In 2016, he had a 1.07 ERA, and in 2017 he had a 1.19 ERA. He signed with the Rangers before the 2018 season. Since 2018, he has pitched in 394 games and posted a 3.26 ERA. He carved out a successful role as a reliever and even received Cy Young Award votes in 2023, when he was a member of the Red Sox. The 40-year-old appeared in 16 games for the Rangers and pitched 14 innings. He had a 9.00 ERA, and now he has decided to hang it up. In 2025, he posted a 2.98 ERA in 49 games, so his falloff was somewhat of a surprise. Regardless, his time in the big leagues has finally come to an end.
